messages.content: I have an old crypto-mining rig: nine NVIDIA P106 cards with 6 GB each, all on PCIe x1 risers, a 2-core Celeron and 4 GB of RAM. I'd like to run a local LLM on it for chatting and some coding help. What should I check or set up first?
Write a bash script that prints each GPU's memory use, temperature and power draw every 5 seconds, and prints a warning line when a card goes above 80 °C.
Why do the x1 risers matter so much when loading a model, but so little when generating text once it is loaded?
Turn the checklist from your first answer into a short table with three columns: item, why it matters, how to check it.

Assuming your first checklist was the pre-flight setup for running a local LLM on that old mining rig, here’s the short version as a table:

| Item | Why it matters | How to check it |
|---|---|---|
| Powered PCIe x1 risers / PCIe power cables | x1 slots have much less bandwidth than x16, and risers need proper power. Model loading can be slow or unstable if power/bandwidth is marginal. | Verify each riser has correct PCIe power cable (6/8-pin) and runs at x1. Test cards one at a time. |
| Motherboard PCIe lane/CPU PCIe controller | x1 bandwidth limits fast model loading; matters most when moving multi-GB models into VRAM. | Check motherboard manual/BIOS; use `lspci -tv`; watch `nvidia-smi` load times. |
| CPU + system RAM (4 GB) | LLM context/KV cache and prompt processing use system RAM. 4 GB is likely too low for comfortable chat/coding use. | Check with `free -h` / `htop`; ideally upgrade to 8–16 GB+ RAM. |
| PSU capacity + cables | Nine GPUs plus risers draw significant power; weak PSU or bad cables cause crashes. | Check PSU wattage; use dedicated PCIe cables per riser; test under load. |
| Cooling / airflow | Poor cooling causes high GPU temps and throttling, especially with passive/small cards. | Check `nvidia-smi` temp/power; clean dust; improve case airflow. |
| BIOS PCIe Gen / slot settings | May run at PCIe Gen1 x1, limiting bandwidth. | Enter BIOS, set PCIe slot to Auto/Gen3 if available, reboot. |
| Drivers / software support | P106 is Pascal-era and needs supported NVIDIA driver + CUDA build for llama.cpp. | Check `nvidia-smi`; use a CUDA-enabled llama.cpp build. |

For the x1 riser question: it matters most **during model loading**, because the model is read from disk/RAM into VRAM over the PCIe bus. Once loaded, generation mostly uses VRAM-to-GPU compute, so the x1 bottleneck is much less of an issue.
Thanks! Summarize the most important points of our conversation in three bullet points.

- The PCIe x1 risers mainly bottleneck **model loading**, because the model data has to move over the narrow bus into VRAM; once loaded, generation is mostly VRAM-to-GPU compute, so the x1 limit matters much less.

- The old mining rig is likely **underpowered for a good local LLM**: the 2-core CPU and only 4GB system RAM are major constraints, along with power, cooling, and PCIe/BIOS setup.

- Before running it, check riser power cables, BIOS PCIe settings, cooling/PSU, and drivers/CUDA support; monitor GPU temps and power, and watch for warnings above **80°C**.

Assuming your first checklist was the pre-flight setup for running a local LLM on that old mining rig, here’s the short version as a table:

| Item | Why it matters | How to check it |
|---|---|---|
| Powered PCIe x1 risers / PCIe power cables | x1 slots have much less bandwidth than x16, and risers need proper power. Model loading can be slow or unstable if power/bandwidth is marginal. | Verify each riser has correct PCIe power cable (6/8-pin) and runs at x1. Test cards one at a time. |
| Motherboard PCIe lane/CPU PCIe controller | x1 bandwidth limits fast model loading; matters most when moving multi-GB models into VRAM. | Check motherboard manual/BIOS; use `lspci -tv`; watch `nvidia-smi` load times. |
| CPU + system RAM (4 GB) | LLM context/KV cache and prompt processing use system RAM. 4 GB is likely too low for comfortable chat/coding use. | Check with `free -h` / `htop`; ideally upgrade to 8–16 GB+ RAM. |
| PSU capacity + cables | Nine GPUs plus risers draw significant power; weak PSU or bad cables cause crashes. | Check PSU wattage; use dedicated PCIe cables per riser; test under load. |
| Cooling / airflow | Poor cooling causes high GPU temps and throttling, especially with passive/small cards. | Check `nvidia-smi` temp/power; clean dust; improve case airflow. |
| BIOS PCIe Gen / slot settings | May run at PCIe Gen1 x1, limiting bandwidth. | Enter BIOS, set PCIe slot to Auto/Gen3 if available, reboot. |
| Drivers / software support | P106 is Pascal-era and needs supported NVIDIA driver + CUDA build for llama.cpp. | Check `nvidia-smi`; use a CUDA-enabled llama.cpp build. |

For the x1 riser question: it matters most **during model loading**, because the model is read from disk/RAM into VRAM over the PCIe bus. Once loaded, generation mostly uses VRAM-to-GPU compute, so the x1 bottleneck is much less of an issue.
